scope: PRISM Cyber Range — pinned component inventory for the design phase (Delivery 1).

license_preference: Apache-2.0 / MIT / BSD / MPL-2.0 (permissive, safe to study and redistribute in docs)
GPL-3.0 / AGPL-3.0 accepted only as isolated services that are never linked into PRISM core
BUSL / SSPL / source-available rejected for anything we depend on
policy.pin_method: container image by tag AND digest, or release tarball by version AND sha256. A tag alone is not a pin.
policy.digest_state: container digests are intentionally null here: they must be resolved and committed on the target host by range/scripts/pin_images.sh at first build, then never changed without a lock diff.
policy.verification_source: GitHub REST API (/releases/latest, /tags) queried 2026-10-31; licences as reported by the same API and cross-checked against each project's docs where noted
policy.unknown_pin_policy: any component whose pin cannot be verified is marked "pin_confidence": "unverified" and may not appear in an acceptance-tested layer

components.role: Hypervisor-adjacent host OS for the whole range
components.name: Debian GNU/Linux
components.version: 12 (bookworm) — or 13 at first build, decision recorded in the install log
components.verified: existing host baseline (D2.5 used Debian 12 successfully)

components.role: Container runtime for layers L1–L4
components.name: Docker Engine (moby)
components.notes: Rootless Podman remains the documented alternative where Docker licensing/daemon model is unwanted; Podman is not pinned yet, so it is an alternative, not a dependency.

components.role: OIDC/SAML identity provider, TOTP and WebAuthn MFA, session and role model
components.name: Keycloak
components.notes: Realistic enterprise IdP with real OIDC token lifetimes, refresh/revocation, WebAuthn and fine-grained roles. Heavy JVM footprint; Tier A uses Authelia instead.

components.role: Lightweight SSO + TOTP/WebAuthn portal for Tier A
components.name: Authelia
components.notes: Same protocol surface (OIDC + TOTP + WebAuthn) at ~5% of Keycloak's RAM. Lacks Keycloak's admin RBAC depth, so role-explosion experiments stay on Tier B.

components.role: Alternative IdP
components.name: Authentik
components.license: reported as NOASSERTION by the GitHub API; core is MIT with separately licensed enterprise features
components.notes: Rejected as default because the licence split must be audited per feature; keeping it in the matrix documents why.

components.role: Internal CA: service mTLS certificates and short-lived SSH user certificates
components.name: step-ca (smallstep)
components.notes: Gives real certificate issuance, CRL/OCSP revocation and short-TTL SSH certs — the mechanisms a revocation drill needs.

components.role: Secrets manager: dynamic DB credentials, PKI, transit, token/session revocation
components.name: OpenBao
components.notes: Vault 2.x is BUSL-1.1 (API reports NOASSERTION), which conflicts with the licence policy. OpenBao is the MPL-2.0 fork with the same API surface, so the lab stays legally clean while teaching the real Vault API.

components.role: Encrypted configuration secrets in git
components.name: SOPS + age
components.notes: Keeps the repository free of plaintext secrets while allowing configuration to be versioned; the age identity lives only on the host. Used at L0 (host bootstrap) and L1 (config injection); tagged L1 because that is where its secrets land.

components.role: Kubernetes control plane for the app/sign/chain workloads
components.name: k3s
components.notes: Real Kubernetes API, RBAC, service accounts and NetworkPolicy without the weight of a full distribution. Tier A runs Compose and forgoes Kubernetes-specific findings — stated explicitly in the fidelity table.

components.role: Alternative Kubernetes distribution
components.name: k0s
components.license: reported NOASSERTION (project uses Apache-2.0 core + some components under other terms)
components.notes: Comparable footprint; kept as the fallback if k3s packaging gets in the way.

components.role: Ephemeral Kubernetes for CI-side policy tests
components.name: kind
components.notes: Only for running Kyverno/OPA policy tests in isolation; never the long-lived lab.

components.role: Network policy enforcement and flow visibility
components.name: Cilium
components.notes: eBPF policy + Hubble flows give the Blue Team real inter-service telemetry instead of synthetic logs.

components.role: Admission policy on the cluster
components.name: Kyverno
components.notes: Realistic guardrail: blocks privileged pods, unsigned images, and hostPath mounts — and gives the Red Team a real policy boundary to test.

components.role: Business authorisation policy for transactions (amount, destination, quorum, velocity)
components.name: Open Policy Agent
components.notes: Rego policy is the same engine class real exchanges use for transaction controls; decisions are auditable and unit-testable.

components.role: Internal source control with real team/permission model
components.name: Gitea
components.notes: Forgejo is the usual alternative but lives on Codeberg, so its releases cannot be pinned from this environment; Gitea is MIT and pinnable here.

components.role: CI runner executing real pipelines with real secrets
components.name: Woodpecker CI
components.notes: GitLab CE would be more realistic but needs ~6 GB RAM alone; Woodpecker keeps the authentic CI-authorisation problem (service accounts, deploy keys, secret scoping) inside the budget.

components.role: Internal image registry
components.name: Distribution (registry:2)
components.notes: Version tag is coarse; the digest resolved on the host becomes the real pin.

components.role: Image and dependency vulnerability scanning in the pipeline
components.name: Trivy

components.role: Secret scanning gate
components.name: gitleaks

components.role: Artifact signing and verification (keyless or key-based)
components.name: cosign (sigstore)
components.notes: Offline key pair only: the lab never reaches the public sigstore transparency log.

components.role: PKCS#11 cryptographic module emulating an HSM (key objects, sessions, CKA_EXTRACTABLE, CKA_SENSITIVE)
components.name: SoftHSM v2
components.notes: The GitHub API exposes no releases for this repository; the pin must be taken from the signed vendor tarball (sha256 + GPG) at build time. This is the single most important fidelity gap in the lab and is treated as such in 08-realism-limits.md.

components.role: Local EVM chain with deterministic state, snapshots and time control
components.name: Anvil (Foundry)
components.version: 1.7.1 (forge/anvil/cast), same build used for D2.5 Stage 1
components.notes: Pinned to the exact toolchain already validated in D2.5 Stage 1 so account artifacts stay comparable with reports/d25-step1/artifacts.sha256.

components.role: Programmable account (ERC-4337 / ERC-6900, incl. EIP-7702 variant) under study
components.name: Alchemy Modular Account v2.0.0
components.notes: Compiled from a read-only checkout; never edited, never vendored. The lab treats it as a third-party dependency whose behaviour is studied, matching the D2.5 constraint.

components.role: ERC-4337 EntryPoint and account interfaces
components.name: eth-infinitism/account-abstraction
components.notes: Exactly the version pinned by the D2.5 target's own pnpm-lock.yaml, so the lab inherits a validated dependency graph instead of inventing a new one. account-abstraction v0.9.0 exists and is deliberately not used (would break comparability).

components.role: ERC-4337 bundler / relayer
components.name: Alto (Pimlico)
components.notes: Maintained TypeScript bundler; eth-infinitism/bundler v0.6.0 (2023) is the fallback and is older than the EntryPoint version in use.

components.role: Network intrusion detection on the zone-to-zone links
components.name: Suricata
components.notes: Sees only what the architecture lets it see; the TLS-coverage limitation is documented rather than hidden.

components.role: Connection/protocol metadata and file extraction
components.name: Zeek
components.notes: The richest source of 'incomplete logs' realism: Zeek's conn/protocol logs are genuinely partial during encryption and evasion.

components.role: Runtime detection in containers/Kubernetes
components.name: Falco
components.notes: Real syscall-driven detection; produces the host-level events a Blue Team must triage.

components.role: Host state inventory and periodic telemetry
components.name: osquery

components.role: Log aggregation
components.name: Grafana Loki
components.notes: AGPL: runs as an unmodified service; no code is linked into PRISM.

components.role: Dashboards and alerting
components.name: Grafana

components.role: Metrics and detection-latency measurement
components.name: Prometheus
components.notes: MTTD/MTTR are only defensible if timestamps come from one clock domain; Prometheus plus a single NTP source is the mechanism.

components.role: Log/metric collection agent
components.name: Grafana Alloy
components.notes: Successor to Promtail/grafana-agent; also the path for shipping Suricata/Falco/osquery output.

components.role: Full SIEM/HIDS alternative (manager + indexer + dashboard)
components.name: Wazuh
components.notes: More realistic SIEM semantics (decoders, rules, CDB lists) but consumes the entire Tier B budget by itself. Documented as the upgrade path, not the default.

components.role: Endpoint forensic collection and hunting
components.name: Velociraptor
components.notes: Gives real VQL collection artefacts instead of hand-written log lines.

components.role: Packet capture and PCAP forensics
components.name: tcpdump / tshark
components.version: host-distribution pinned versions (recorded in the install log)
components.notes: Distribution-pinned; the exact versions are written into the install log at build time so runs remain reproducible. Used at L6 (capture) and L7 (PCAP forensics); tagged L6 as the capture point.

rejected.name: HashiCorp Vault
rejected.reason: BUSL-1.1 licence conflicts with the open-source-only policy; OpenBao provides the same API under MPL-2.0.

rejected.name: HashiCorp Terraform
rejected.reason: BUSL-1.1; OpenTofu v1.13.5 (MPL-2.0) is the drop-in alternative if infrastructure-as-code is adopted in L2.

rejected.name: Security Onion
rejected.reason: Needs 16 GB+ RAM minimum for a usable deployment; excluded from all tiers but kept in the matrix as the ceiling reference.

rejected.name: GitLab CE
rejected.reason: 6 GB+ RAM alone; the same CI-authorisation findings are obtainable with Gitea + Woodpecker at ~0.5 GB.

rejected.name: Cloud HSM / real HSM
rejected.reason: Cost and third-party dependency; explicitly out of scope. SoftHSM emulation is documented as the fidelity gap, not papered over.
